facebook.long_form:
🥎 **LLSWS DAY 4 RECAP + THE SHOWDOWN THAT'S HAPPENING RIGHT NOW**

Day 4 at Stallings Stadium in Greenville eliminated two more teams and set up the most anticipated game of the tournament so far.

Wednesday morning, Washington (Snohomish, WA) took care of Canada 9-1. Madison Locke was everything — 6 innings, 4 hits, 1 run, 0 walks, 12 strikeouts. Janessa Malone went 3-for-3 with 2 RBI. Canada is eliminated.

Wednesday afternoon, Toms River, New Jersey's Mid-Atlantic squad finished what Day 1 started. Japan (Sangō, Asia-Pacific) had beaten them 4-1 on opening day. On Day 4, Toms River returned the favor — 11-0 shutout in what was supposed to be an elimination game for the NJ team. Japan is eliminated. Toms River avenged their loss and moved on.

Now here's today's story:

Lake Mary, Florida (Southeast) and Clayton, North Carolina (the NC host team) are both 2-0. They play each other TODAY at 1 PM ET on ESPN. Lake Mary has run-ruled two opponents and outscored the field 29-0. Clayton is the host team from Johnston County making their first-ever LLSWS run — they won 16-4 over Canada and 2-1 over Texas. Neither team has given up a run.

One of them is about to.

---

stories.title: Team Watley Wins the AUSL Pro Game 6-2 at Stallings Stadium

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text:
Team Watley 6, Team Fernandez 2.

The AUSL Pro Game at Stallings Stadium is official — Natasha Watley's squad beat Lisa Fernandez's team Wednesday night on ESPN2.

Next up: the AUSL All-Star Cup starts this Saturday in Rosemont, IL.

45 players. 12 games. 🥎

#AUSL #Softball

facebook.long_form:
🥎 **TEAM WATLEY WINS THE AUSL PRO GAME — AND THE ALL-STAR CUP IS THIS SATURDAY**

Wednesday night at Stallings Stadium in Greenville — while the Little League Softball World Series was on a brief pause — the AUSL Pro Game delivered exactly what it was supposed to be.

Team Watley defeated Team Fernandez 6-2 in a full nine-inning exhibition. Twenty-four of the best softball players in the world, split into two teams wearing their regular-season AUSL uniforms, coached by Natasha Watley and Lisa Fernandez. The final box score: Watley 6 runs, 7 hits, 1 error; Fernandez 2 runs, 5 hits, 3 errors.

The context made it better than any final score can capture. These players had spent Tuesday at the LLSWS games, doing first pitches and meet-and-greets with the competing teams. Wednesday morning they ran a youth Tee Ball clinic for two local Little League programs. Then that night, they played in front of the LLSWS crowd — kids who had been competing in the same stadium all week, now watching the best softball players in the world.

That's the whole point of it.

What's next: the 2026 AUSL All-Star Cup starts this Saturday, August 8, in Rosemont, Illinois — and runs through August 30. Forty-five players, 12 games broadcast on ESPN, MLB Network, and CBS Sports Network. If you enjoyed the Pro Game, the All-Star Cup is the longer version.

---

facebook.long_form:
🥎 **SEPTEMBER 1 IS 26 DAYS AWAY — AND THE CLASS OF 2028 IS THE BIGGEST EVER EVALUATED**

Extra Inning Softball has received 1,226 nominations for the Class of 2028 — the most in their company's history. Not by a little. More than any previous class.

Those 1,226 names represent players who went through PGF Nationals, major showcases, the LLSWS, summer tournaments — everything on the 2026 evaluation circuit. Division I coaches across the country have been watching. They've seen the film, logged the stats, compared the scouting reports. The summer is done.

September 1 is when it becomes real. That's the day D1 coaches can pick up the phone and call a Class of 2028 prospect directly for the first time. Before that date, they can receive questionnaires and attend events, but they cannot initiate contact. The first call from a program is a significant signal — it tells a prospect where she stands in that staff's priorities.

For a record class of prospects, September 1 is 26 days away.

The coaches know who they're calling. The prospects don't.

---

✅ Pickering — .384 career BA, 50 HR (OU)
✅ Heavener — 13-9, 2.81 ERA (LSU)

No. 1 transfer class. 2026 WCWS Finalists. Zero games together yet. 🥎

#Softball #SoftballRecruiting

facebook.long_form:
🥎 **TEXAS TECH 2027 — HERE'S WHAT THE ROSTER ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE**

For five days, the coverage of Texas Tech's transfer class focused on one name at a time. Jaysoni Beachum. Then Kasidi Pickering. Then Jayden Heavener. Now let's put it together.

**What Texas Tech is adding:**
- Jaysoni Beachum (from FSU): .406 average, 10 HR, 69 RBI; 2024 NFCA Freshman of the Year; 2026 2nd-Team All-American
- Kasidi Pickering (from OU): .384 career average at Oklahoma; 50 home runs, 169 RBI in 186 games; .370 average with 20 HR and 61 RBI in 2026 alone; 2024 national champion and WCWS All-Tournament selection
- Jayden Heavener (from LSU): 13-9 with a 2.81 ERA in 2026; two full years of eligibility remaining

**What they're returning:**
Texas Tech already reached the 2026 Women's College World Series Finals. They already had a top-five caliber offense. Now they add one of the most prolific hitters in recent college softball history (Pickering), a proven FSU star who was an impact freshman before she learned the game (Beachum), and pitching depth that was the one gap in their title picture (Heavener).

This class hasn't played a game together yet. Fall camp starts in a few weeks. By the time the 2027 season opens, a Texas Tech win column built on these pieces could look like anything.

---

stories.title: USA WNT's Next Challenge — WBSC World Cup Group C Qualifier in Oklahoma City

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
USA Softball won International Cup gold on August 3.

Next stop: the WBSC World Cup Group C qualifier — September 12 in Oklahoma City.

Same venue. Same USA WNT.

37 days to the next one. 🥎🇺🇸

#USASoftball #Softball

facebook.long_form:
🥎 **USA SOFTBALL WON THE INTERNATIONAL CUP. HERE'S WHAT'S NEXT.**

Three days ago, Montana Fouts carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning of the International Cup gold medal game and beat Japan 2-0 at Devon Park in Oklahoma City. USA WNT claimed gold.

The next milestone on the calendar: the WBSC Softball Women's World Cup Group C qualifier — September 12-16, 2026 — in Oklahoma City. Same venue. Same national team program. Different tournament, with World Cup qualification on the line.

Winning the International Cup was the summer showcase. The World Cup qualifier is the pathway. USA softball's international calendar doesn't stop after one gold medal. For a team with 2028 Olympic ambitions, every tournament between now and Los Angeles is meaningful — and the Group C qualifier is 37 days away.

The WNT has won the gold. Now they go earn what comes next.

---
